title: Updating working memory in aircraft noise and speech noise causes different fMRI activations

findings.antecedent: substitution processes (adding new items to WM and suppressing old items)
findings.consequent: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), posterior medial frontal cortex, and parietal lobes activation
findings.mechanism: frontal-parietal network associated with manipulation/change of WM representation; cognitive conflict detection
findings.quote: the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), the posterior medial frontal cortex and the parietal lobes were more activated by 'substitution' trials

findings.antecedent: exclusion processes ('no substitution' trials, rejecting new items and maintaining intact memory set)
findings.mechanism: cognitive conflict detection; inhibition of prepared substitution response to irrelevant stimuli; excluding potentially relevant stimuli
findings.quote: the anterior medial frontal cortex was more activated by 'no substitution' trials than by 'substitution' trials.

findings.antecedent: task performance with speech noise in background (vs. silence)
findings.consequent: bilateral but left-lateralized temporal cortex (Left superior temporal gyrus, Right superior temporal gyrus) activation
findings.quote: doing the task with speech as a background noise... activated the bilateral but left-lateralized temporal cortex

findings.antecedent: task performance with aircraft noise in background (vs. silence)
findings.consequent: left temporal cortex (Left superior temporal gyrus) activation
findings.quote: doing the task with aircraft noise as a background noise... activated only the left temporal cortex

findings.antecedent: task performance with speech noise in background (vs. aircraft noise)
findings.mechanism: semantic referents in speech automatically activate cognitive processes
findings.quote: the left middle temporal gyrus was activated more by speech than by aircraft noise

findings.antecedent: task performance with aircraft noise in background (vs. speech noise)
findings.consequent: basal structures of the right temporal lobe and cerebellum (Right postcentral gyrus, Right supramarginal gyrus, Right cerebellum 6) activation
findings.mechanism: different acoustic characteristics and frequency distribution of sound types
findings.quote: aircraft noise did activate any areas more than speech did at the chosen alpha levels. Reducing the alpha level to p < 0.05 to explore sub-threshold effects revealed activation in the basal structures of the right temporal lobe and cerebellum

findings.antecedent: substitution trials with speech noise in background (vs. aircraft noise)
findings.consequent: medial PFC (middle cingulate and supplemental motor area), right central gyrus, and bilateral temporal areas (Right precentral gyrus, Right postcentral gyrus) activation
findings.mechanism: background speech requires more cognitive control and active inhibition to prevent interference; medial PFC associated with excluding task-irrelevant materials
findings.quote: trials requiring updating processes undertaken with speech in the background are associated with a greater activation in the medial PFC

findings.antecedent: substitution trials with aircraft noise in background (vs. speech noise)
findings.consequent: occipital, temporal and anterior parietal regions (Left inferior parietal gyrus, Left superior parietal gyrus, Left precuneus, Right superior parietal gyrus, Right inferior parietal gyrus, Right angular gyrus, Left superior frontal gyrus, Left precentral gyrus, supplemental motor area, Left precentral gyrus, Left middle frontal gyrus, Left inferior frontal triangularis, Right superior frontal gyrus, Right middle frontal gyrus, Left crus cerebellum, Left caudate, Left thalamus, Right middle frontal gyrus) activation
findings.mechanism: involvement of visual imagery (visuo-spatial sketchpad) to perform the task, relying more on visual imagery when speech noise interferes with phonological loop
findings.quote: 'substitution' trials undertaken with aircraft noise in the background caused more activation in the occipital, temporal and anterior parietal regions

findings.antecedent: background noise conditions (silence, speech noise, aircraft noise)
findings.mechanism: participants increased mental effort to compensate for interference
findings.quote: t-test comparisons were not significantly different (all p > 0.5).

findings.mechanism: task was understood and WM operations were performed as expected
findings.quote: The participants' performance on responses indicating whether or not they updated their WM content had a high accuracy across trial types (overall accuracy, M = 95%, SD = 21.7%).

stimuli.description: aircraft noise recorded near an airport
Norwegian male actor reading a meaningful, correctly structured, fictitious story with non-salient content
visual double-digit numbers (15-99) presented as white text on a black background

tables.description: Clusters of voxels significantly more activated in the contrasts of interest, including anatomical localization and Brodmann areas

limitations: The scanner environment did not allow the participants to report their actual memory content.
Behavioral measures may not be sensitive enough to detect differences when participants compensate by increasing mental effort.
